nodes.text:
Wait. It doesn't say that at all. It says that... 

Getting the flu vaccine did not make people in this study more likely to catch other viruses (this is what "virus interference" refers to—when vaccination might theoretically increase susceptibility to other infections).

The flu vaccine seemed to slightly increase the chance of catching certain viruses like coronavirus (not necessarily COVID-19) and human metapneumovirus. (maybe 36% is slight?)

On the other hand, the flu vaccine provided protection not only against most flu strains but also against other respiratory infections like parainfluenza, RSV (respiratory syncytial virus), and some cases where people had more than one virus at the same time.

So, while the flu vaccine might have a small link to increased risk of a couple of specific viruses, it generally provides broad protection against the flu and some other respiratory infections.
